title: Export settings: JPEG, WebP and TIFF with presets, resizing and optimisation
objective: Deliver an Export sheet with Web, Print and Master presets and the person's own, exporting JPEG, lossy WebP and 8/16-bit TIFF with resizing, optimised encoding, file-size limits and metadata levels through one ExportSettings API, then output sharpening, with declared-tolerance GPU correctness and recorded measurements.
context_summary: The owner requested a plan with UX designs (2026-10-07) and chose: JPEG, WebP and TIFF (no DNG); lossy WebP; a sheet that writes directly into its folder with an editable suffix; output sharpening after the core delivery. The owner decided on 2026-10-08 that optimisation and file-size limits have no memory cap, with a large-image warning in the sheet and a progress bar for long exports. Other defaults (preset values, preset storage, Lanczos-3, Annex K tables, the 24 MP warning threshold, the progress-bar rule, metadata levels, shortcuts) are recorded proposals in the design; routine layout and code organisation are delegated. Implementation is not authorized by the planning request. No external inputs block delivery: generated 24/60 MP JPEGs and supplied RAW fixtures suffice; missing native Windows/Linux GPU evidence stays unrun. Re-review against current main and use the roadmap high-tier model minimum. The design, docs/design/export-settings.md, is the contract for every task; its boards are in docs/design/export-settings/.

tasks.description: Define ExportSettings, export presets and the export API: export.plan with settings, export.write replacing export.jpeg, batch.export with settings, export.presets.* and the remembered last export.
extra_context: Deliver the settings type, validation, output-size arithmetic, name rule, metadata levels, preset store and command registrations consumed by TASK-005 and TASK-006. Rendering and encoding stay today's (full-size baseline JPEG) until TASK-005 wires the new paths; settings a format or renderer cannot honour yet are refused by name, never ignored.

Fields, ranges and per-format applicability are the design's Settings table; a field that does not apply to the chosen format is a validation error naming it. Output size scales both sides by one factor never above 1 and rounds to whole pixels; null pixels_per_inch keeps today's desktop density behaviour.

export.plan answers stage and output size, physical size, the suggested path from folder and suffix counting up within 64 names, the encoder's held-memory estimate, and notices with codes (large-image above 24 MP of optimised or size-limited output, with the estimate; webp-too-large; folder-missing). It renders nothing. export.write keeps export.jpeg's freeze, request-id retry and job semantics and validates the destination's extension against the format. Remove export.jpeg and its desktop callers in the same change (current shapes only).

Built-in Web, Print and Master presets are constants listed first; the person's presets live in export-presets.json beside preferences.json in the host configuration directory, at most 100, names unique case-insensitively, an unreadable or unsupported document kept and refused by name. export_last replaces the export_folder preference and is stored only after a successful person-started export.

Metadata levels select from the existing supported field table: none, copyright (Artist, Copyright), no_location (everything but the GPS group), all. Structural fields are written for every level but none.
Implementer owns module layout, error wording and schema prose within the design.

Output sizes match an independent calculation for portrait, landscape, cropped and rotated stages and every fit with bounds above, at and below the stage; nothing is enlarged.

tasks.description: Add JPEG quality, chroma and Optimise options to luxforge-jpeg, with the coefficient-memory limit and a bounded limit-file-size search.
extra_context: Deliver encoder options consumed by TASK-005: quality 1-100, chroma 4:4:4 or 4:2:0, and Optimise (progressive scans, optimised Huffman tables, trellis quantisation) while keeping the standard Annex K quantisation tables for both settings, so a quality value means the same with Optimise on or off.

mozjpeg's set_fastest_defaults and scan-optimisation setters call jpeg_set_defaults and reset quality, sampling and density: call them first. Trellis has no safe-wrapper setter; use the pinned mozjpeg-sys parameter API if needed.

Every optimisation allocates whole-image coefficient arrays (two in mozjpeg). There is no memory cap (owner, 2026-10-08): Optimise applies at every size. Expose a pure estimate of that memory for export.plan. Install libjpeg's progress monitor (jpeg_progress_mgr through mozjpeg-sys if the safe crate lacks it) to report determinate progress across passes, and check cancellation between passes without unwinding through C frames. Optimise off stays the current streamed encoding and its byte-for-byte behaviour.

Limit file size: an in-memory encode of a held frame of any size bisecting quality downward from the requested value, at most eight encodes, returning the best fitting result and the quality used, or a refusal when nothing fits at quality 10. Report each attempt as progress and check cancellation between attempts.
Update the existing SOF0/4:4:4/standard-DHT assertions to cover each option rather than deleting them.

tasks.description: Add lossy WebP and 8/16-bit TIFF encoders with ICC and metadata, behind the export encode interface.
extra_context: Deliver encoders consumed by TASK-005. WebP: pinned libwebp-sys with vendored C source and its mux API; lossy 4:2:0 at a quality, Optimise as the slowest method with sharp RGB-to-YUV; ICCP and EXIF chunks; refuse outputs over 16,383 px a side before encoding. It encodes a whole picture and must accept a borrowed frame without a second full copy where the API allows.

TIFF: pinned tiff crate; RGB 8 or 16 bits per channel written by strips as rows arrive; Optimise as lossless Deflate with the horizontal predictor if the pinned version supports it, otherwise the implementer records the measured alternative; ICC in tag 34675, descriptive fields in IFD 0, capture fields in an Exif IFD and GPS in a GPS IFD from the existing metadata model.
Limit file size applies to WebP through the same bisection contract as JPEG (shared helper with TASK-002 is the implementer's choice).
Record each new dependency, its licence and its native build in docs/engineering/dependencies.md and keep cargo-deny passing; do not claim a licence audit.

tasks.description: Render resized and 16-bit export output on the reference renderer and the GPU tile worker, and add both export kinds to gpu-qualification with the design's declared limits.
extra_context: Deliver render paths consumed by TASK-005: an output size below the stage and an output encoding of 8 or 16 bits per channel.

Reference: resample the exact whole frame in linear light with a separable Lanczos-3 whose support scales with the reduction, clamped, then encode once; exact-buffer tests against a stepwise reference. The output frame is bounded by the stage and the 512 MiB evaluated-frame limit.

GPU: resampling is the stream's final staged sweep from content-stage textures inside GPU_TILE_BUDGET, cutting output bands of the output's width; a stage that does not fit is the reference's (tiles-budget). 16-bit bands are read back at 16 bits per channel. Keep two bands in flight, cancellation between tiles and the whole-export reference restart when a stream stops.

Declared limits: resized and 16-bit exports within the stack class's display limit (four statistics over every pixel) against the reference's resized or 16-bit export, ΔE00 computed from the 16-bit values. A cell past its limit is a defect to fix, not a reason to loosen the limit.
Run qualification for these kinds here on the corpus subset needed to prove the path; the full corpus run and measurements belong to TASK-008.

tasks.description: Integrate settings, encoders and render paths into export.write and batch.export, with phases, results and refusals as designed.

tasks.description: Build the desktop Export sheet, Export menu, Export again and Export with preset, and Select's batch sheet, with a rendered journey and current documentation.
extra_context: The first useful delivery. Follow the boards in docs/design/export-settings/ and the design's sheet behaviour; reuse the Settings sheet's scrim and stacking and the existing segmented, toggle, slider and number-field widgets. Leave the Sharpen row out entirely until TASK-007.

The sheet is a client: readouts, suggested names and notices come from export.plan, asked only on format, size, density, folder or suffix changes, one in flight with the newest pending. No asset.state, history refresh, preview job or upload is added; job reads use the existing reader stream.

Large images: the sheet shows the amber large-image notice from export.plan under Quality (batch mode counts photographs over the threshold), never blocking. The status bar shows a determinate bar with phase and percent from the start for a warned export and otherwise once the job's elapsed time passes one second, derived from the existing job reads with no new timer; clicking it opens the Performance section with Cancel.

Menu: Export… (Cmd+E), Export again as Preset (Shift+Cmd+E, disabled until an export succeeds), Export with preset entries; palette entries per preset and Export reference render… opening the sheet with reference true. Select's Export N… opens the sheet in batch mode instead of the folder dialog.
Changed-preset marking, Save as preset…, Update, Rename, Duplicate and Delete go through export.presets.*. Status lines report size, bytes and quality used as designed.
Update export.md, features.md, user-guide.md, decisions.md and the smoke scenario table for delivered behaviour only; sharpening stays described as planned.
Automated launches use the hidden background bundles; no foreground interaction check is required.
